source.title: Hyaluronic Acid: A Key Ingredient in the Therapy of Inflammation

source_integrity_notes: This source is a narrative review; cited-study effects are secondary reports and were not encoded as primary-study quantitative_result atoms.

No systematic search strategy, study-selection flow, formal risk-of-bias assessment, or evidence-certainty framework is reported in the article body; this is an appraisal limitation, not a reported-data atom.
All model-extracted atoms remain needs_review because no independent human reviewer step is represented.
No external current-practice verification was performed; the 2021 review is not treated as current clinical guidance.

semantic_spot_checks.source: Conclusion states reviewed studies show promising results for HA in inflammatory pathologies while identifying delivery limitations.
semantic_spot_checks.artifact: ATOM conclusion/limitations and SEA conclusion preserve both promise and delivery constraints.

semantic_spot_checks.source: Introduction reports HMWHA usually >1000 kDa; degradation section reports compartment-specific half-lives; hydration section reports up to 10,000× water binding.
semantic_spot_checks.artifact: Corresponding review-synthesis atoms preserve these magnitudes without treating them as review-generated primary data.

semantic_spot_checks.source: Conclusion identifies short biological-fluid half-life, potential crosslinking toxicity, viscosity, and need for more studies.
semantic_spot_checks.artifact: All are represented explicitly in ATOM and SEA.

semantic_spot_checks.source: Table 1 spans 20 OA formulations; Table 2 has 12 RA formulations; Table 3 has 5 wound-healing rows; Table 4 has 6 IBD rows.
semantic_spot_checks.artifact: SEA structurally reconstructs all rows and ATOM records table-level secondary evidence patterns.
